info.description:
# Premisave backend

Requests for every Premisave microservice, grouped by service. Import this collection together with the **Premisave Local** environment, select the environment, then follow the quick start.

## Quick start

1. Select the **Premisave Local** environment and fill in `email` and `password` (and the `base_url_*` values if your ports differ).
2. Run **Auth Service > Authentication > Sign up**, open the activation email, copy the token from the link into `verification_token` and run **Verify email**. Skip this if the account exists.
3. Run **Auth Service > Authentication > Sign in (email and password)**. The test script saves `token`, `refresh_token`, `session_id` and `my_user_id`.
4. Run anything else. Every request uses the saved token automatically.

## Services and base URLs

| Folder | Variable | Local default |
|---|---|---|
| Auth Service | `base_url` | `http://localhost:8080` |
| Listing Service | `base_url_listing` | `http://localhost:8082` |
| Wallet Service | `base_url_wallet` | `http://localhost:8084` |
| Messenger Service | `base_url_m_service` | `http://localhost:8085` |
| Property Service | `base_url_property` | `http://localhost:8086` |
| C2B Hakikisha Service | `base_url_c2b_hakikisha` | `http://localhost:8087` |

Only the auth (8080) and wallet (8084) ports come from the services' own configuration. Change the others to match your setup.

## How authentication works

- The collection sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` on every request. Requests that must be public (sign in, sign up, recovery links, health) are set to **No Auth**, and requests with their own header (for example `X-API-Key`) keep it.
- The token is a JWT issued by the auth service. All services accept it because they share `JWT_SECRET`.
- Access tokens can be short-lived (`SECURITY_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES` on the auth service). A **collection pre-request script** renews the token with `refresh_token` about a minute before it expires, so long test sessions keep working. Each refresh token works once and is replaced.
- **Sign out**, **End one session** and **End all other sessions** make the matching tokens stop working immediately in the auth service.
- Service-to-service endpoints (`/internal/**`) use `X-API-Key: {{internal_api_key}}`. One value must be set in every service.

## Variables

Variables are filled in three ways:

- **You set them** (environment): base URLs, `email`, `password`, `new_password`, `internal_api_key`, OAuth tokens, provider test keys.
- **Scripts set them** (dynamic): `token`, `refresh_token`, `session_id`, `other_session_id`, `my_user_id`, `my_role`, `device_id`, `device_token`, `application_id` and `document_id`. The Property Service scripts also save the ids it creates (`property_id`, `unit_id`, `lease_id`, `tenant_id`, `payment_reference` and the rest of its ids). Ids in the other services (listing, wallet and so on) are pasted from a response.
- **You paste them from an email**: `verification_token` (activation), `reset_token` (password reset), `invitation_token` (admin invitation), `security_action_token` ('This wasn't me').

Scripts write to the selected environment, or to the collection variables when no environment is selected.
`user_id` and `target_id` are for acting on other users and are never overwritten by a script. `my_user_id` is your own id.

## Scripts

- **Collection pre-request:** renews an expiring access token (see above).
- **Collection tests:** every response is checked for no 5xx and a response time under 5 seconds, and a 401 or 403 prints a hint to the console.
- **Property Service folder:** a pre-request script gives each payment a `payment_reference`, and tests save the ids it creates and print a hint for 401, 403 and 503 responses.
- **Request tests:** sign in, refresh, sign out and the security calls assert the status and shape of the response and save ids for the next request. Open the Postman console to see what each script did.

## Naming and order

- Requests are named verb first, sentence case: *List my active sessions*, *Revoke device trust*.
- Within the Auth Service the folders follow the user journey: sign in, protect the account, profile, social, location, applications, administration, internal, health.
- In every service the system and health folders come last.
- Folder descriptions list their endpoints with method, path and auth.

## Testing recipes

- **New-device alert:** sign in, then delete the `ps_did` cookie for the auth host in Postman's Cookies manager and sign in again. The account receives an alert email with a 'This wasn't me' link.
- **Lock-out:** send **Sign in** with a wrong password five times. The sixth answer is `429`. A wrong password and an unknown email always return the same `401` message.
- **Session revocation:** sign in twice (second time after deleting the cookie), then **List my active sessions**, **End one session**, and call any endpoint with the old token to see `401`.
- **'This wasn't me':** copy the token from the alert email into `security_action_token`, run **inspect** (changes nothing), then **confirm**. Running confirm again fails because the token is single use.
- **Pay rent:** sign in as the home owner and the tenant (**Sign in by role**), then follow the Property Service folder description (suggested order). Fund the tenant's wallet first, run **Pay rent on a lease**, and send it again with the same `payment_reference` to see that a retry is not charged twice.
- **Admin provisioning:** set `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS`, restart the auth service, open the invitation email, put its token in `invitation_token` and run **Accept admin invitation**, then sign in.

## Security notes

- Do not store real passwords, API keys or provider secrets in the collection. Put them in the environment, mark them secret and do not share the environment file. Provider secret keys that were in an earlier version of this collection should be rotated.
- The earlier hardcoded admin credentials were removed. There is no default admin account.

| 403 | Correct password but the account is unverified or deactivated |
| 429 | Temporarily locked after repeated failures. Lock time grows with repeated locks |

**What happens behind the scenes**

- A new or untrusted device triggers a sign-in alert email with a 'This wasn't me' link.
- The device is remembered by an HttpOnly cookie (`ps_did`). Postman keeps it, so repeat sign-ins from Postman look like a known device. Delete the cookie in Postman's Cookies manager to test the new-device alert.
- A configured admin address is promoted to ADMIN here if it has not been already.

item.name: Rent Payments
Get rent due on a lease

request.description:
Pays rent on a lease from the tenant's wallet. The service makes one transfer to the owner's wallet and books the payment only after that transfer succeeds. If the lease needs a security deposit that is not held yet, part of the payment goes to the deposit first (see `depositAmountApplied` in the response).

`paymentMethod` accepts only `WALLET` (or leave it out). `amount` is USD, positive, at most 2 decimal places.

**`reference`** makes the payment retry safe. Reuse the same value to retry a payment that failed or timed out and it is never charged twice. The folder's pre-request script fills `payment_reference` with a new value when it is empty, and the test script clears it after a successful payment so the next payment gets a new one.

**503** means nothing was charged (`SERVICE_OFFLINE`, auth or wallet service down) or the outcome could not be confirmed. In both cases send the request again with the same `reference`.

- **Owner requests** (create a property, manage units and leases, send notices, blacklist, inspections, reports and so on) send `{{home_owner_token}}`. Run **Auth Service > Authentication > Sign in by role > Sign in as home owner** first.
- **Admin requests** (**List all leases as admin** and **Get health details**) send `{{admin_token}}`.
- **Everything else** sends `{{token}}`. Sign in as the tenant to run the tenant requests. The Auth column of each folder says who may call a request.
- To test with a single account, put its token in `home_owner_token` as well, or change a request's Authorization tab.

Access is checked per record, not only by role. An owner reaches only their own properties and the leases, units and tenants tied to them, and a tenant reaches only their own lease, unit and payments. A record that does not exist is a **404**, and a record that belongs to someone else is a **403**. A missing or expired token is a **401** with `code` `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` or `SESSION_EXPIRED`.

## Money

Every amount is **USD** with at most 2 decimal places and must be positive. Rent, utility and deposit payments are wallet transfers: fund the tenant's wallet in the Wallet Service first. Pay requests take a `reference`, so a retry never charges twice.

## Scripts

- **Folder pre-request:** the pay requests get a new `payment_reference` when it is empty.
- **Folder tests:** ids from create responses are saved for the next request (`property_id`, `unit_id`, `rental_unit_id`, `lease_id`, `tenant_id`, `owner_id`, `maintenance_id`, `maintenance_request_id`, `work_order_id`, `inspection_id`, `notice_id`, `scheduled_notice_id`, `meter_reading_id`, `bill_id`, `deposit_id`). A successful payment clears `payment_reference`, a failed one keeps it so the retry is safe. The console explains 401, 403, 503 and a switched-off token check.

## Folder order

The folders follow the life of a tenancy: **Owners**, **Tenants**, **Properties**, **Rental Units**, **Leases**, **Occupancy**, **Rent Payments**, **Security Deposits**, **Meter Readings**, **Utility Bills**, **Maintenance**, **Work Orders**, **Inspections**, **Notices**, **Blacklisted Tenants**, **Dashboard and reports**, **System**. Inside a folder, requests go from create to list, get, update and delete. Requests are named verb first, in sentence case.

## Suggested order

1. **System > Check dependency status**, to see that the authentication and wallet services are up.
2. As the owner: **Owners > Create owner profile from my account**, **Properties > Create property**, **Rental Units > Create rental unit**.
3. As the tenant: **Tenants > Create tenant profile from my account**.
4. As the owner: **Leases > Create lease**, then **Occupancy > Record move-in on a lease**.
5. As the tenant: **Rent Payments > Pay rent on a lease**.
